author: JaffaBeard
body: Burnout is very real and you should definitely allow yourself a break from playing. It's happened to me a few times over the years and taking time off helped. Personally when I found it getting too grindy I would start looking at my achievements and see what I was close to completing. Setting smaller goals like, codex filling, fishing, areas. Looking at my local ranking and seeing if I can jump up the leader board. Looking up gear upgrades and targeting them through Raids or dungeons. Even jumping through someone's Wayvessel who have specific themed dungeons can break things up. Chaos scrolls for Yeti hunting is a gamble but could pay off if you get a decent Overcoat drop. But yeah, if you feel burnt out take a break.

author: NoShadowdick
body: If you feel burnt out, then take a break. I took a nice 6 to 8months break from the game after hit t10. Came back feeling good a day ready to hit 250.

author: Widogeist
body: The Orna community is one of the highlights of the game IMO; kingdom and group/co-op play adds a different dynamic to the game which can be refreshing if you've mostly been playing solo since day 1.  The game itself is inherently grindy and trust me it won't get better, if anything it'll get worse as you progress into higher tiers.  Setting smaller goals, engaging in the community, and joining a Kingdom are good starting points.  But don't force yourself to play if you are getting burned out, taking a break is healthy and sometimes necessary.  As a 250 player myself, one thing that keeps me interested in the game is testing out different builds/playstyles and theorycrafting new setups; I love the PvP side of Orna, and I find it fun when new builds are discovered.

author: VanZandtVS
body:
There's nothing wrong with taking a break if you're burned out.  

If you don't feel like logging in once a day to fight your wars it'll be best to leave your current kingdom, unless your kingdom mates just don't care about the loss if you get matched up.  There's nothing preventing you from rejoining your group if you've enjoyed playing together. 

I feel like the game really changes once you get to level 225.  Suddenly you're collecting gear you'll use for the rest of your tenure in game and to me that just makes everything feel much more relaxed.  It's like there's a mad scramble to get to that point but once you do suddenly the game opens up. 

Also, as others have pointed out, one of the best parts of Orna is the community.   I've been playing with the same core group of kingdom mates for almost 3 years, and I definitely would have taken more breaks had it not been for them and the kingdom discord.

author: Odeken
body: Totally normal it took me over a year to get 225 because of burn out, but the game will always call you back! Once you get level 190+ish the grind starts to hit making burn out easier.

author: Delois2
body: The community is a large part of this game, join discords, find an active kingdom and get yourself a goal. It just gets more grindy from here, but imo, that's a feature. Even the best players in the game still have things to grind for.

author: ShadowyShroom
body:
I'm about to hit 225 later today. I've taken 2 or 3 breaks in my journey to T10. Personally, I just don't worry about doing things optimally. I like min-maxing my gear, but I don't think too much about events, statues and stuff like that. I just play the game in a relaxing way, and I like to think back when some bosses required several deaths to defeat that I now 1-shot.

For me, Orna feels like a nice journey, and I just don't stress about anything. But seriously, it's okay to take breaks. I took a 1 year long break when I was at your level, and now that I am in a kingdom, I have periods of tile where I log in once a day, just to get rewards and do kingdom wars/gauntlets. Now I'm playing actively again. As long as you have fun, you do you :)

author: petr1petr
body:
when people burn out, they will quit for some time - some will return, some will not.

This game is about grind - you will have hard time if you dont enjoy grind.. Community helps a lot - if you get lucky to join good kingdom and if you are interested in game, it will help a lot. also, if you can make someone around you play and meet with them, that helps even more.. 

or maybe getting more involved in the game could help - like making your own kingdom and managing it.. 

as for "waiting for random ornate" - rumors are talking about 1/200 chance for ornate - so pretty slim chance - people usually hunt for good equips - doing a lot of gautlets or raids to get desired item - on the other hand, people also get lucky and gain great items for very little work - like my alt, who deals next to no dmg on raids and still has some items better than my main.. so it is not impossible - just - dont rely on it..

author: StDimi
body: T7 is most likely the moment when most people let go, then come back or not. This is probably the most boring moment in the game. After u got lvl 175, the dungeons are starting to be 20 floors, you start to feel that the new T8 class (175-199) is starting to mean something as you finally choose your way to the first T10 class. Later on on T9 things get even more interesting as you have access to "most" of the content in the game. (chance for godforge, first endgame items, access to almost all dungeons). After that, getting to t10 is tiring and time-consuming, but there is a chance that someone will help you if you have a nice kingdom, or enough summoning scrolls :D
